accepted.title: Integral virtual algebraic fibring from vanishing over every prime field
accepted.text: Fix n≥0 and a residually finite rationally solvable (RFRS) group G of type FP_{n+1}(Z). Is the existence of a finite-index subgroup H≤G with an epimorphism H→Z whose kernel is of type FP_n(Z) equivalent to b_i^{(2)}(G;F_p)=0 for every prime p and every 0≤i≤n? Here FP_j(R) means that the trivial R[G]-module has a projective resolution finitely generated through degree j. For an RFRS group, b_i^{(2)}(G;F_p)=dim_{D_p}H_i(G;D_p), with D_p the unique Hughes-free division ring generated by F_p[G].
accepted.subject: Group Theory & Geometric Group Theory

accepted.title: Virtual specialness versus virtual free-by-cyclic structure for one-relator groups
accepted.text: Is a one-relator group G virtually free-by-cyclic if and only if it is virtually special? Here one-relator means a finite presentation with a single defining relator; virtually free-by-cyclic means that some finite-index H≤G fits into 1→F→H→Z→1 with F free, not assumed finitely generated. Virtually special means that a finite-index subgroup is the fundamental group of a special nonpositively curved cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise.

accepted.title: Group coherence versus coherence of its group algebra
accepted.text: For every group G and field k, is G coherent if and only if k[G] is coherent? A group is coherent if every finitely generated subgroup is finitely presented; a ring is coherent if every finitely generated one-sided ideal is finitely presented as a module (for group algebras, left and right coherence are equivalent).

accepted.title: Universal Hughes-free division rings for torsion-free one-relator groups
accepted.text: For every torsion-free one-relator group G and every field k, does k[G] admit an epic embedding into a division ring D which is both Hughes-free and universal? Hughes-free means that D is generated by k[G] and, for every N◁H≤G with H finitely generated and H/N≅Z, distinct powers of a lift of a generator of H/N are left-linearly independent over the division closure of k[N] in D. A k[G]-division ring is epic if the image of k[G] generates it as a division ring; it is universal if its matrix-rank function dominates that of every epic k[G]-division ring (equivalently it admits a specialization to each, in the sense of a homomorphism from a suitable local subring).

accepted.title: Universality of Hughes-free division rings for locally indicable 3-manifold groups

Must its Hughes-free division ring D_{k[G]} be universal as an epic k[G]-division ring? Locally indicable means that every nontrivial finitely generated subgroup surjects onto Z. Hughes-free means that D is generated by k[G] and, for every N◁H≤G with H finitely generated and H/N≅Z, distinct powers of a lift of a generator of H/N are left-linearly independent over the division closure of k[N] in D. A k[G]-division ring is epic if the image of k[G] generates it as a division ring; it is universal if its matrix-rank function dominates that of every epic k[G]-division ring (equivalently it admits a specialization to each, in the sense of a homomorphism from a suitable local subring).

Hughes-free means that D is generated by k[G] and, for every N◁H≤G with H finitely generated and H/N≅Z, distinct powers of a lift of a generator of H/N are left-linearly independent over the division closure of k[N] in D. A k[G]-division ring is epic if the image of k[G] generates it as a division ring; it is universal if its matrix-rank function dominates that of every epic k[G]-division ring (equivalently it admits a specialization to each, in the sense of a homomorphism from a suitable local subring).

excluded.scope_review: All torsion-free groups and all field characteristics are retained. The unit conjecture, particular 3-manifold groups and the stronger division-ring embedding conjecture are different targets.
excluded.literature_finding: The current Fisher–Sánchez-Peralta publication still identifies the general zero-divisor conjecture as open, while resolving 3-manifold groups. Unit-conjecture counterexamples do not supply zero divisors.
excluded.reason: Fisher: a domain means exactly no nonzero factors with ab=0. All fields and torsion-free groups match.
Exact full equivalence is already Q2428. The March 2026 RFRS theorem is a restricted theorem with a virtual nonpositive-immersion caveat, not an unrestricted closure or a new question.

The thesis’s positive-characteristic L² invariants require a Hughes-free embedding for a locally indicable finite-index subgroup, but the candidate quantifies arbitrary lattices in SO(n,1). That defining scope has not been cleared for arbitrary higher-dimensional lattices. Do not silently restrict to simple-type/cubulated lattices or substitute ordinary mod-p homology growth.

Resolved by Coherent RFRS groups (March 2026), Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 4.1. For RFRS G with cd_Q≤2, vanishing b₂^(2) gives homological coherence over Q; each finitely generated subgroup is then coherent by Corollary 4.1, hence FP₂(Z). Conversely, homological coherence over Z implies that over Q, and Theorem 1.2 gives vanishing. The finitely generated condition in Corollary 4.1 is applied separately to each subgroup, so the deduction covers the source’s general G.

The question refers to the particular embedding produced by a graph-of-rings/Cohn construction. The source theorem only asserts an embedding, while a canonical universal division-ring choice and its epic closure need to be stated to make the three Linnell/Hughes-free/universal obligations standalone. The current published Lemma 7.6 identifies the construction if Hughes-free existence for the whole group is already assumed; it does not resolve the full combination question. Held for a precise construction-choice review, rather than fabricating the ring D.
